messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing sporadic p99 spikes on llama-3-13b in the chat path when chat-padding is enabled. spikes only show up at batch==1 and seq in 600..900 range.
sanjay: Any recent infra or runtime changes?
maya: No big deploys. Repro locally with the bench harness. minimal command: `./bench --model llama3-13b --seq 768 --batch 1 --chat-pad 96 --profile`
maya: Profiler top lines:```
timeline: tokens 1-36: attn_fused_fast (3.4ms)
token 37: packer::align -> kv_ptr += 16 -> kv_stride 320->336 -> selector falls back
selector picks: scalar_multihead_slow (11.9ms)
stack: packer::align -> kv::realloc_if_needed -> selector::choose -> scalar_attn
```
kevin: That ptr +16 shift smells like a packing padding change, maybe from the fused SiLU param buffer we added last quarter.
sanjay: rope_theta? our defaults changed across Llama2/3 catalog entries and "auto" can compute different scales which affect pos-embedding tensor math.
maya: Forcing `--rope_theta 4096` or `--rope_theta 8192` removes the fallback in my runs. With explicit rope_theta we stay on attn_fused_fast for full sequence.
kevin: So two plausible mechanisms: (A) the computed rope embedding expansion changes allocation size/rounding; (B) SiLU/RMSNorm fused extra buffer shifts base pointer. Both cause kv_stride misalignment.
perf-bot: job/RUN-6241 completed: p50 3.3ms, p95 39ms, p99 121ms, traces: /perf/RUN-6241
ops-bot: host/cpu-ax-11: mem pressure low, no OOMs. runtime:v1.83.14.
kevin: Quick experiments I ran:
- zeroing the temporary SiLU buffer before allocation removes the +16 shift and keeps fast kernel.
- forcing quantized kernel for batch==1+chat-pad>0 also stayed on fast-ish codepath (p99 improved).

sanjay: Quant fallback seems like a short-term mitigation but we need to be careful: quant path is not identical numerically. Can we gate behind a canary?
maya: Proposed action plan: 1) add deterministic diagnostic logging in packer (base_ptr % 64, computed kv_stride, head_dim, required_alignment_bits) when selector chooses slow path; 2) run micro-bench matrix: chat_pad {0,32,64,96,128} x rope_theta {auto,4096,8192}; 3) implement a feature-flagged selector_relaxed_align which downgrades alignment requirement (32->16) as an experiment; 4) canary quant-fallback for batch==1/chat-pad>0.
kevin: I'll add the packer logs and do the bench matrix today. I'll also prototype relaxing the alignment check behind ff:selector_relaxed_align.
perf-bot: created perf job: RUN-6242 (micro-bench matrix).
sanjay: We should also verify head_dim invariants: Llama3-13b has head_dim 128, but our stride calc includes interleaved params for fused activations so effective_head_stride can change. Log effective_head_stride too.
maya: Good call. Also add an invariant assert in debug builds that logs if head_dim % 32 != 0.
kevin: If packer logging confirms pointer shifts by small deltas, likely short-term patches are safe. Long term we should remove implicit padding in the fused param allocation or ensure all allocations use an alignment helper.
maya: I'll file INF-5230 with the repro, traces, and proposed mitigations. linking logs and perf traces there.
ops-bot: ticket INF-5230 created and linked to RUN-6241/RUN-6242.
sanjay: Canary plan for selector change: dev bench -> internal canary 2% traffic for 1hr -> 10% for 2h -> full rollout. For quant fallback: start at 1% due to numeric risk.
maya: Thanks — I'll post updates in this thread as the micro-bench results come in. :mag:
